claims.text: The initial alloy is a W-Mo-Ta-Nb refractory high-entropy alloy.
The intervention is addition of Al, Cr, and Si to the W-Mo-Ta-Nb alloy.
Adding Al, Cr, and Si promotes formation of a dense oxidation film.
A dense oxidation film improves high-temperature oxidation resistance.
Introducing refractory elements W, Mo, Ta, and Nb enhances mechanical properties.
Introducing refractory elements W, Mo, Ta, and Nb enhances thermal stability at elevated temperature.
The hypothesis should hold in an oxidizing atmosphere above 900 °C.
The Al-Cr-Si-modified alloy will form a dense oxidation film under the stated conditions.
Refractory elements will precipitate in the modified alloy.
W-Mo-Ta-Nb can form a BCC solid solution.
W, Mo, Ta, and Nb precipitate as strengthening phases that improve mechanical properties.
The Al-Cr-Si-modified alloy will have better high-temperature oxidation resistance than the unmodified W-Mo-Ta-Nb baseline.
The modified alloy will have greater strength than the unmodified baseline.
The modified alloy will have greater hardness than the unmodified baseline.
The modified alloy will have greater thermal stability than the unmodified baseline.
The baseline has the same refractory W-Mo-Ta-Nb composition but contains no added Al, Cr, or Si.
The proposed mechanism and outcome are limited to W-Mo-Ta-Nb-based RHEAs and may not apply to other HEA systems.
Failure of the modified samples to improve oxidation resistance over the unmodified control would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: W, Mo, Ta, and Nb are already the constituents of the initial and baseline alloy, while the hypothesis and mechanism describe their 'introduction' as a source of improvement; the stated intervention actually introduces only Al, Cr, and Si.

Mechanical and thermal improvements are predicted relative to the baseline, but they are attributed to refractory constituents present in both baseline and modified alloys rather than to the Al-Cr-Si intervention. No supported mechanism connects the actual intervention to those comparative outcomes.
